notes:
Lead source: inbound self-serve signup (trial started Mar 8). Small engineering team (14 engs), product lead is CTO-level. Primary ask: quick guidance on which hosted model variants to use during POC and expected cost/latency tradeoffs.

Summary of conversation (Mar 11 discovery):
- Wants hosted API only for now (no VPC/private). Prefers self-serve path but wants short checklist.
- Workloads: chat-based customer support assistant (priority) + embeddings for doc search and a small code-assistant prototype.
- Traffic profile: initially light (peak ~8-12 RPS conversational bursts), monthly tokens estimate ~80k-150k during POC. Cost sensitive — target: keep monthly inference spend < $1k during POC.
- Latency target: 150-300ms per token on average for chat; will accept higher initial latency if cost is low.
- Model questions: asked directly about Llama vs Mistral vs Qwen variants and quantized flavors. Key asks were: "Which gives best quality for support + code while keeping token costs low?" and "How much do 7B quantized variants degrade vs 13B unquantized?"

Technical notes / advice given on call:
- Recommended starting experiments: Mistral-7B/standard hosted and Llama-2-13B-quantized (if available) + Qwen-7B for code probing. Rationale: Mistral-7B often provides strong quality/cost ratio for instruction chat; Qwen-7B shows strengths on code tasks; Llama-13B quantized can provide a safer-guard on semantics for tougher threads.
- Discussed quantization tradeoffs: 4-bit/INT4 variants reduce cost ~2.5-4x but may lose subtle instruction-following for complex prompts — advise running small eval set from their past support transcripts.
- Gave ballpark per-token cost examples (hosted):
  * Mistral-7B hosted: lower cost baseline (example: $0.0006/token write estimate for planning) — good for iterating prompts.
  * Qwen-7B hosted: similar to Mistral for cost, slightly better on code samples (empirical).
  * Llama-13B (unquantized): higher cost and latency; quantized 13B variants reduce spend but test for hallucination/regression.
- Suggested test plan for POC (2 weeks):
  1) Run 500 representative support prompts through Mistral-7B and Qwen-7B on hosted API (compare avg latency, token usage, quality).
  2) If quality gap significant on edge cases, trial Llama-13B-quantized for those threads.
  3) Use Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + prefix caching) to estimate cost savings — especially for high-reuse prompt prefixes in support.
